provenance.status: Original procedural reconstruction; not a retail mesh reproduction.
provenance.dimensions: Authored estimates in metres; not measured stock data.
provenance.rig: Guide-based authored family interpretation. Stock sail-plan/locator geometry was unavailable.
provenance.gun_layout: Authored symmetric broadside allocation of the verified stock total. z_m is the row centre at zero sheer; the builder adds the authored local deck sheer. This is not a claim about stock gun locators.
provenance.stock_script_caveat: Pinned stock-derived modern compatibility scripts are not authenticated byte-identical retail source.

source_evidence.claim: Family, model identifier, class and total cannon count only.
Ordinary family identity; no dimension or sail-plan data.
General game visual vocabulary only: pale panelled square canvas, dark wales and ochre hull bands. The pictured family is not authenticated.
Authored hull/port/mast proportion method and rig distinctions; not stock game dimensions.
Square/lateen/gaff typology and spar proportion starting points; later brig is not the reference Snow.

type_profile.distinction: Fuller three-masted 38-gun galleon with high forecastle, two stepped stern castles, square fore/main rigs and a long lateen mizzen.
type_profile.rationale: High castles, broad afterbody and lateen mizzen are the authored earlier galleon type cues. Gun-row distribution is an authored allocation of the stock total, not a recovered game-locator list.

scope.delivered: Static duel asset with two paint variants and LOD/collision/review assets.
scope.engine_integration: Not integrated with an engine: no buoyancy, damage, artillery, sailing or crew controllers.
scope.walking: Authored geometric passage and stair access; no player controller or engine navigation integration. Actual clearance checks are recorded in validation.json after build.
scope.interiors: Modelled structural interiors with real planked decks, frames, hatch apertures, stairs and cabin partition openings. Layout is an authored reconstruction, not recovered retail geometry.

evidence.title: Vasa Museum: precise dimensions and levels of Vasa
evidence.kind: Museum research interpretation of surviving seventeenth-century ship
evidence.observed: Vasa has hold, orlop and two gun decks, plus several sterncastle levels. Published clear heights vary by location, and some upper after rooms are low.
evidence.application: Real separate hold/orlop/lower-battery levels; stepped after accommodation beneath the preserved high castles.
evidence.limit: Swedish warship analogue, not a Spanish trading galleon or the POTC Galleon. We enlarge authored access passages and do not copy the published clear heights.

evidence.title: Vasa Museum: Life on board
evidence.kind: Museum exhibit based on surviving archaeological objects
evidence.observed: The museum distinguishes the upper gun deck, helm and great cabin in its full-scale reconstructions and cross-section model.
evidence.application: A distinct furnished after cabin, physical helm context and visible gun-deck structure.
evidence.limit: Room furniture is an original interpretation, not a reconstruction of Vasa or unknown POTC interiors.

evidence.title: Fundación Nao Victoria: History of the Galleon
evidence.observed: The foundation describes Spanish galleons as armed ocean-going trading ships with several decks; its El Galeón replica interprets that family.
evidence.application: Preserve high castles and mixed cargo, battery and after-accommodation roles.
evidence.limit: The modern replica uses a modern construction core; it is an arrangement analogue, not evidence of traditional internal scantlings or exact stock model geometry.

notes: Two retained batteries, high aftercastles and lateen mizzen remain distinct from the later frigate. Lower orlop and hold are real planked spaces. Main great cabin sits abaft the last lower battery station; low upper aftercastles are stores/chart spaces rather than invented full-height decks.
The authored cabin-front partition is placed aft of the preserved mizzen and its complete doorway approach; the centered 1.15 m door and main-hatch connection remain full-size.

The authored stern joinery uses four symmetric cabin lights around a solid central rudder post, preserving the original rudder hardware; the count and placement are fitted design choices, not recovered retail or museum-plan coordinates.
